join.description: How a stroke's corners are drawn.

keys.description: Morph keys: the shape takes each path at its time, morphing between (matching point counts morph point for point).

at.description: Seconds on the node's composition clock.

anyOf.description: Continuous bezier keys: one speed (units per second) on both sides of each key, derived from its neighbours when left out, with handles inInfluence and outInfluence of the segments around it (1/6 by default). autoBezier derives the speed from the keys either side; numbers only.

path.description: SVG path data at this key.

node.description: A node's id: ids are unique in the document, so a node inside a composition is named by its id alone. A path through instances (scene.1/title) is accepted too.

paint.description: Fill the path's inside, stroke its line, or both.

MotionCommandSetPath.title: setPath

MotionCommandSetProperty.description: Sets a property. On an animated property `at` is required and sets the key there; without `value` it adds a key holding the value at `at`. `blendMode`, `flipX` and `flipY` are set without `at`.

at.description: Where to set it when the property is animated: the key there is added or changed. Required then.

node.description: A node's id: ids are unique in the document, so a node inside a composition is named by its id alone. A path through instances (scene.1/title) is accepted too.

property.description: A property name (x, y, scale, rotation, opacity, volume, …) or a field:… path; inspect_motion_node_properties lists a node's.

value.description: Left out, a key at `at` holding the value the property has there.

MotionCommandSetProperty.title: setProperty

MotionCommandSetShape.description: Changes a shape's kind, box, colour or corner radius.

box.description: Where a rect or circle draws, px in its composition; a circle fits the box's smaller side, centred. A rect or circle keeps its box when left out.

color.description: #rrggbbaa for a see-through fill; #00000000 makes a shape whose backdrop effects adjust what is beneath it.

node.description: A node's id: ids are unique in the document, so a node inside a composition is named by its id alone. A path through instances (scene.1/title) is accepted too.

shape.description: fill covers its composition; rect when box is given.

MotionCommandSetShape.title: setShape

MotionCommandSetSpeed.description: Plays a node faster or slower (0.05 to 20).

node.description: A node's id: ids are unique in the document, so a node inside a composition is named by its id alone. A path through instances (scene.1/title) is accepted too.

MotionCommandSetSpeed.title: setSpeed

MotionCommandSetTextAnimation.description: Animates a title per character, word or line as it comes in or goes out. `preset: null` removes it.

duration.description: Seconds each unit takes (0.4 by default).

from.description: Which units go first; start by default.

node.description: A node's id: ids are unique in the document, so a node inside a composition is named by its id alone. A path through instances (scene.1/title) is accepted too.

phase.description: in as the title appears; out ends as the title ends.

stagger.description: Seconds between units' starts (0.04 by default).

unit.description: What animates one at a time; character by default.

MotionCommandSetTextAnimation.title: setTextAnimation

MotionCommandSetTimeRemap.description: Replaces a media node's or composition instance's timing with keys of which source time shows when: slow motion, speed ramps and freeze frames (`hold`). Media plays forward only.

keys.description: Replaces the node's timing with these keys (media forward only; an instance can reverse); null restores it.

easing.description: Into the next key; hold freezes the frame.

source.description: The media's (or instance's composition's) time shown there.

node.description: A node's id: ids are unique in the document, so a node inside a composition is named by its id alone. A path through instances (scene.1/title) is accepted too.

MotionCommandSetTimeRemap.title: setTimeRemap

MotionCommandSetTitle.description: Changes a title's text, box, font, size, colour or spacing.

align.description: Within the box's width; center for a new title.

box.description: Where the text lays out, px in its composition: x, y the top-left of the first line's box (fontSize × lineHeight tall, glyphs sit inside it by their font's metrics), width what it wraps and aligns in.

color.description: Text colour; white for a new title.

font.description: A font from list_motion_fonts: a catalog slug, e.g. inter, or a font uploaded to your library or your workspace's by its id (mi_…).

letterSpacing.description: Added between characters, in em: 0.05 is 5% of the font size. 0 for a new title.

lineHeight.description: A multiple of the font size; 1.2 for a new title.

node.description: A node's id: ids are unique in the document, so a node inside a composition is named by its id alone. A path through instances (scene.1/title) is accepted too.

text.description: What it says; `Title` for a new title.

weight.description: 100 (thin) to 900 (black); list_motion_fonts gives each font's range, and a font draws the nearest weight it has.

MotionCommandSetTitle.title: setTitle

MotionCommandSetTransition.description: Sets the transition into a sequence child from the child that ends where it starts.

duration.description: Seconds, 0.5 by default; never longer than either child.

kind.description: crossfade dissolves; left, right, up and down wipe in that direction; none removes the transition.

node.description: The sequence child the transition leads into; another child must end where it starts.

MotionCommandSetTransition.title: setTransition

MotionCommandSplit.description: Splits a node in two at a time.

at.description: Where to split, on the node's composition clock.

newNodeId.description: The second half's id; generated when left out.

node.description: A node's id: ids are unique in the document, so a node inside a composition is named by its id alone. A path through instances (scene.1/title) is accepted too.

MotionCommandSplit.title: split

MotionCommandStagger.description: Starts each node `interval` seconds after the one before, moving their keys and effects with them.

interval.description: Seconds between one node's start and the next's.

nodes.description: In the order they start; each moves with its keys and effects.

items.description: A node's id: ids are unique in the document, so a node inside a composition is named by its id alone. A path through instances (scene.1/title) is accepted too.

start.description: Where the first starts; where it starts now when left out.

MotionCommandStagger.title: stagger

MotionCommandTrim.description: Moves a node's start or end. A new start trims the head: what plays stays put.

node.description: A node's id: ids are unique in the document, so a node inside a composition is named by its id alone. A path through instances (scene.1/title) is accepted too.

ripple.description: In a sequence, the node keeps its start and what follows moves by as much as its length changes.

start.description: The new start; what plays stays put.

MotionCommandTrim.title: trim

MotionCommandUngroup.description: Puts a group's nodes back in its place. A moved group leaves a hidden null they follow; a clipped or filtered group is refused.

node.description: A node's id: ids are unique in the document, so a node inside a composition is named by its id alone. A path through instances (scene.1/title) is accepted too.

MotionCommandUngroup.title: ungroup

MotionComposition.description: A composition's node outline and the instances that play it. Editing a composition changes every instance.

MotionDocument.description: A Tella Motion document: a render timeline (a tree of media, sound, text, shape, sequence and composition nodes) that a Tella Motion clip, overlay or b-roll plays live, so edits show in the video at once.

ownerID.description: The owner's ID: the video's, for `story` documents; yours, for `user` documents.

sceneID.description: The clip that plays this document, when it is a Tella Motion clip's. Absent for overlays and b-roll.

scope.description: Who owns the document: `story` for a video's own documents (its Tella Motion clips, overlays and b-roll), `user` for one of yours that no video plays yet.

MotionDocumentDownload.description: The whole document as stored (`formatVersion`, `name`, `timeline`: the render timeline with every node, composition and asset, and `editor`: names, colours, locks and other editor state by node path) and `seq`. Its shape is `GET /v1/motion/schema?schema=document`. Times are ticks, whole units of 1/`timeline.canvas.ticksPerSecond` s: divide by it for seconds.

MotionDocumentSummary.description: The document's canvas, the outline of its nodes (paths, types, windows in seconds, what they show, paint order, transitions), its compositions and assets, the editor's node names, colours, mute, solo and locks, and `seq`, the revision to pass as baseRevision.

MotionEdit.description: One edit in a batch: an editor command (camelCase `type`, times in seconds) or an op (dotted `type`, raw render timeline values). See https://docs.tella.com/mcp-tools/motion-commands for every command and op with an example.

MotionEffectsResponse.description: The effect kinds the `addEffect` command takes

effect.description: With `kind`: that effect, its presets with their values; with `preset` too, that preset's `params`.

effects.description: Without `kind`: each effect kind (blurs, glows, shadows, colour grading, keying, distortion, wipes, path effects, echo, repeater) with its parameters' names, types, ranges, units and defaults, its presets by name and description, and `presetsKeep`, the parameters a preset leaves as they are.

fonts.description: The catalog's fonts, by the slug a title takes.

libraryFonts.description: The fonts uploaded to your library or your workspace's, by the id (`mi_…`) a title takes, with the weight of each file of a family.

MotionMediaResponse.description: The videos, sounds and images already in the document, each with the `mediaId` the `addMedia` command places.

MotionNode.description: One node with every stored field, its window, the composition it sits in and, for an instance, the outline of the composition it opens. Its fields hold stored values, so their times are ticks (divide by `timeline.canvas.ticksPerSecond` for seconds); its window is in seconds.

MotionNodeProperties.description: A node as the editor's inspector shows it at a time: every animatable property with its unit, range, value there and keyframes (time, value, easing), its effect stack and expressions, its style (blend, flips and shadow), title or shape settings and audio fades. Times are seconds, except the motion blur shutter, which is stored ticks (unit `ticks`).

type.description: The op: what the document stores, with render timeline values. `GET /v1/motion/schema?schema=edits&type=…` gives each one's fields.

MusicBeatsResponse.description: Tempo, beats and bars of a music track, analyzed once per track and cached

beatsMs.description: Every beat, in ms: on the video's playback timeline for background music (the same times as `get_timeline`), in source time for a source

beatsPerBar.description: Beats in each bar: 4, or 3 for a waltz-like meter

bpm.description: Tempo in beats per minute. 0 when the track has no beat at all

confidence.description: How clearly the track has a pulse, 0 to 1. Steady produced music is usually above 0.4; beatless ambient music below 0.1, where the beats are only a guess

downbeatsMs.description: The first beat of every bar, a subset of `beatsMs`. Cut or start a motion on these for the strongest musical accents

durationMs.description: Length of the timeline the beats are on: the video's playback duration for background music, the source's duration for a source

trackDurationMs.description: Length of one pass of the track. Background music restarts after it, so its beat grid restarts too

OverlayAnimation.description: How the overlay enters and leaves, like the editor's Animate panel. When set it replaces `transition`.

intro.description: How the whole overlay enters, or null when it appears instantly.

motionBlur.description: Blur the overlay along its motion while it moves, scales or turns.

outro.description: How the whole overlay leaves, or null when it disappears instantly.

textIntro.description: How a text overlay's letters, words or lines enter, one after another, while `intro` plays on the whole box. Null when they don't.

textOutro.description: How a text overlay's letters, words or lines leave, one after another, while `outro` plays on the whole box. Null when they don't.

OverlayAnimationCurve.description: How a side accelerates. `linear` keeps one speed. `smooth`, `natural`, `slow_down`, `accelerate`, `elastic`, `bounce`, `overshoot`, `impulse` and `swing` are shaped by `intensity`. `custom` follows `bezier`, `spring` follows `spring`.

intensity.description: How strongly the curve shapes the motion, 0 to 1. Only curves with an intensity use it.

OverlayAnimationEasingInput.description: How the side accelerates. Without it a new side slows down into place on the way in and speeds up on the way out.

bezier.description: For `custom`: the handles. Defaults to the side's current curve.

intensity.description: How strongly the curve shapes the motion, 0 to 1. Only curves with an intensity use it. Defaults to 0.5.

spring.description: For `spring`: its physics. Defaults to stiffness 200, damping 12, mass 1.

OverlayAnimationInput.description: How the overlay enters and leaves; when set it replaces `transition`. Each side describes the hidden state the overlay moves from on the way in and back to on the way out. An omitted side stays as it is. `{intro: {preset: 'slide_up'}, outro: {preset: 'fade'}}` is a complete animation; on text, `{textIntro: {preset: 'slide_up', text: {unit: 'words'}}}` brings the words in one by one.

intro.description: How the whole overlay enters, or null to appear instantly. Takes no `text`. Omit to keep the current intro.

motionBlur.description: Blur the overlay along its motion while it moves, scales or turns. Defaults to true.

outro.description: How the whole overlay leaves, or null to disappear instantly. Takes no `text`. Omit to keep the current outro.

textIntro.description: Text overlays only: how its letters, words or lines enter, one after another, or null for none. Plays alongside `intro`: both start together.

textOutro.description: Text overlays only: how its letters, words or lines leave, one after another, or null for none. Plays alongside `outro`: both end together.

OverlayAnimationPreset.description: A ready-made side, the same as the editor's Animate presets. A `slide_*` or `mask_*` arrow is the direction the overlay travels, so a `slide_up` intro rises into place and a `slide_up` outro rises away.

OverlayAnimationSide.description: One side of an overlay animation: the hidden state the overlay moves from on the way in, or back to on the way out.

blur.description: Blur of the hidden state in pixels.

clip.description: Clip the motion to the overlay's box, so it wipes in like a mask.

durationMs.description: How long the side plays, in ms (50 to 5000). On a text side, how long each unit plays.

moveX.description: Horizontal offset of the hidden state, as a fraction of the overlay's width (of a line's height on a text side); positive is right.

moveY.description: Vertical offset of the hidden state, as a fraction of the overlay's height (of a line's height on a text side); positive is down.

opacity.description: Opacity of the hidden state, 0 to 1.

preset.description: The preset the side matches, or null once its motion is custom.

rotate.description: Clockwise rotation of the hidden state in degrees.

scale.description: Scale of the hidden state; 1 is its resting size.

OverlayAnimationSideInput.description: One side of an overlay animation. A side starts from its `preset` (or from the side as it is) and the fields you give adjust it.

blur.description: Blur of the hidden state in pixels.

clip.description: Clip the motion to the overlay's box, so it wipes in like a mask.

durationMs.description: How long the side plays, in ms (50 to 5000). On a text side, how long each unit plays. Defaults to 500.

moveX.description: Horizontal offset of the hidden state, as a fraction of the overlay's width (of a line's height on a text side); positive is right.

moveY.description: Vertical offset of the hidden state, as a fraction of the overlay's height (of a line's height on a text side); positive is down.

opacity.description: Opacity of the hidden state, 0 to 1.

preset.description: Start from a ready-made side; the other fields adjust it. Without it the side starts from what it is now; a new whole side starts still and a new text side from `fade`.

rotate.description: Clockwise rotation of the hidden state in degrees.

scale.description: Scale of the hidden state; 1 is its resting size.

OverlayAnimationSpring.description: Spring physics. The spring sets the side's `durationMs`: it lasts until the spring comes to rest.

OverlayAnimationSpringOutput.description: Spring physics. The spring sets the side's `durationMs`: it lasts until the spring comes to rest.

OverlayAnimationText.description: The units a text side plays on, each in turn.

delayMs.description: How long after one unit the next starts, in ms (0 to 2000).

order.description: Which unit goes first. `random` uses the same shuffle every time.

smoothing.description: Eases the delays across the units: `linear` is an even step, the other curves bunch the starts up at one end.

OverlayAnimationTextInput.description: On `textIntro`/`textOutro` only: which units play the side, each in turn. Required on a new text side.

delayMs.description: How long after one unit the next starts, in ms (0 to 2000). Defaults to 100.

order.description: Which unit goes first. `random` uses the same shuffle every time. Defaults to `forward`.

smoothing.description: Eases the delays across the units. Defaults to `linear`.

OverlayDepth.description: Where the overlay sits relative to the presenter: the person in the clip's camera recording, or in its uploaded footage when the clip has no camera. `front` paints over everything. `behind_presenter` paints it behind the person but over everything else: in any layout the person is matted out of their footage and redrawn above the overlay. Fullscreen and framed layouts keep the recorded room around them; a cut-out layout replaces the room with the clip background. New overlays start on `front`. Without a presenter the overlay paints in front either way.

OverlayDepthChanges.description: Changes of `depth` over the overlay's own time, each held until the next: `atMs` after the overlay starts it moves to that depth, so one overlay can pass in front of the presenter and back behind them (a ring orbiting their head, a title they step in front of). `depth` is where it starts. On updates, omit it to leave the changes as they are; `[]` removes them. Absent in responses while the overlay holds one depth.

OverlayDimensions.description: Overlay size in artboard pixels. Absolute (not a percentage) so the overlay shape never distorts when the artboard dimensions change. Both sides must be greater than 0 — the renderer lays the overlay out into this box, so a zero or negative side has no valid meaning.

OverlayDimensionsOutput.description: Overlay size in artboard pixels. Absolute (not a percentage) so the overlay shape never distorts when the artboard dimensions change. Both sides must be greater than 0 — the renderer lays the overlay out into this box, so a zero or negative side has no valid meaning.

OverlayPoint.description: Top-left corner of the overlay, as a percentage of the video canvas (0-100). Relative so the anchor survives video aspect ratio changes.

OverlayPointOutput.description: Top-left corner of the overlay, as a percentage of the video canvas (0-100). Relative so the anchor survives video aspect ratio changes.

OverlayZIndex.description: Stacking position among the clip's image, video and text overlays: 0 is the backmost. `depth` applies first — a `behind_presenter` overlay stays behind the presenter whatever its zIndex — so the order only matters among overlays at the same depth. Lottie overlays share the stack but aren't listed, so listed values can skip a number.

Pagination.description: Pagination metadata for list responses. Results are sorted by updatedAt descending.

hasMore.description: Whether there are more items to fetch

nextCursor.description: Cursor for next page. Pass this value as the 'cursor' query parameter to fetch the next page. Null if no more pages. This is an opaque value - do not decode or modify it.

description.example: A collection of tutorial videos for our product

emoji.description: Unicode emoji character for the playlist

groupId.description: Playlist group this playlist belongs to in the sidebar, or null if ungrouped

searchEngineIndexingEnabled.description: Whether search engines can index this playlist

videos.description: Number of videos in the playlist

visibility.description: Whether playlist is shared with org or personal to creator

PlaylistGroup.description: A sidebar group that playlists can be organized into. Personal groups are only visible to you; org groups are shared with the whole workspace.

emoji.description: Unicode emoji character for the group, empty if unset

visibility.description: Whether the group lives in the personal or workspace section of the sidebar

PlaylistGroupVisibility.description: Visibility: org (shared sidebar group for the entire organization) or personal (only visible to you)

PlaylistLinkScope.description: Access level: public (anyone with link), private (only invited users, plus the workspace when visibility is org), password (requires password), embedonly (only viewable when embedded)

viewPage.description: URL to view the playlist on Tella

PlaylistListItem.description: Playlist item in a list response

description.example: A collection of tutorial videos for our product

emoji.description: Unicode emoji character for the playlist

groupId.description: Playlist group this playlist belongs to in the sidebar, or null if ungrouped

searchEngineIndexingEnabled.description: Whether search engines can index this playlist

videos.description: Number of videos in the playlist

visibility.description: Whether playlist is shared with org or personal to creator

PlaylistVisibility.description: Visibility: org (shared with entire organization) or personal (only creator)

accountId.description: The connected account it was published with; null for publishes made before Tella supported several accounts

captionsError.description: Set on a completed YouTube publish whose caption track was refused

destination.description: One of the request destinations, or tiktok

error.description: Why a failed publish failed and what to do next, as a sentence for people. Never the destination's raw response

scheduledAt.description: When a scheduled publish goes out; null when it wasn't scheduled

status.description: A scheduled publish stays `queued` until its time, and is `cancelled` if taken back before then

url.description: The post on the destination, once completed

accountId.description: Which of your connected accounts to post with, from GET /v1/social-accounts. Defaults to the oldest connected account for the destination.

description.description: YouTube description, or the post text on LinkedIn, X, Instagram and Facebook.

destination.description: Where to post. YouTube Shorts must be vertical or square and at most 3 minutes; Facebook Stories vertical and at most 60 seconds; Facebook Reels vertical and at most 90 seconds; Instagram Stories at most 60 seconds and 100 MB; Instagram posts and reels at most 15 minutes and 300 MB; no Instagram destination takes a 4K export; LinkedIn at most 30 minutes and 500 MB. Instagram, Facebook Stories and Reels and LinkedIn need at least 3 seconds. YouTube takes at most 15 minutes from a channel that isn't verified; X at most 20 minutes, or 125 with Premium or a checkmark. Stories show no text. The Facebook and Instagram destinations publish through one Facebook connection.

export.description: Settings of the export to upload, as POST /v1/videos/{id}/exports takes them. A finished or running export with these settings is reused; otherwise one is started. Defaults to 1080p, 30 fps, no burned-in subtitles, 1x.

privacy.description: YouTube: private (default), unlisted or public. LinkedIn: private (connections only, default) or public. Facebook posts: private (only people who manage the Page, default), unlisted (anyone with the link) or public. Facebook posts, stories and reels go to the default Page set in Settings → Connections, else the first Page the account manages. Instagram destinations likewise go to the default Instagram account. Every other destination: public only.

scheduledAt.description: When to post, as an ISO 8601 time with a timezone, e.g. 2026-10-20T15:00:00Z; at most 30 days ahead. The video is exported now, so later edits aren't in the post. Omit to post as soon as the export is ready.

title.description: Video title on YouTube. On LinkedIn, X, Instagram and Facebook it is the post text when description is empty.

uploadCaptions.description: YouTube only: upload the transcript as a caption track (default true). Skipped when the export has burned-in subtitles.

url.description: Opens the user's recorder for a new clip at the end of the video. It needs the user to be signed in to Tella.

videoId.description: The video the recording is added to

RemoveSilencesRequest.description: Options for removing silences from a clip

mode.description: How aggressively to remove silences: natural cuts pauses longer than 800ms, fast longer than 500ms, faster longer than 300ms. Defaults to natural.

ReorderClipRequest.description: Move a clip to a new position. Other clips are renumbered to keep ordering contiguous.

order.description: New position for the clip (0 = first)

reason.description: What went wrong, in the user's words when they gave them: what the take shows against what was asked, or how the recording plays. Never a password, code or sign-in link.
reason.example: It opened the settings page instead of the invoice it was asked to show.

SaveSubtitlePresetRequest.description: A subtitle look to save. Pass `videoId` to snapshot a video's current subtitles, `captionStyle` to build one from scratch, or both — explicit caption fields override the video's.

captionFontFamily.description: One of Tella's catalog font families or the built-in subtitle families `Dela Gothic One`, `Lato`, `Georgia`, and `Arial`. Defaults to the video's font, or the style's default face.

captionFontSize.description: Exact subtitle text size, 40 to 200. Defaults to the video's, or the style's default. Pass this or `captionSize`, not both.

captionFontWeight.description: Subtitle font weight, 100 to 1000. Catalog fonts clamp to their supported range; built-in subtitle fonts outside the catalog snap to an available weight. Defaults to the font's current weight.

captionGrouping.description: How subtitle text is grouped: sentence chunks or one word at a time. Defaults to the video's, or chunked.

captionLinesPerBlock.description: Lines per chunked caption block: 1, 2, 3, or 0 for no limit. Defaults to the video's, or 1.

captionPosition.description: Normalized subtitle position, or null for automatic placement. Defaults to the video's, or automatic.

captionSize.description: Subtitle text size. Defaults to the video's, or the style's default. Pass this or `captionFontSize`, not both.

captionStyle.description: Subtitle style for the preset. Required without `videoId`; with it, replaces the video's style.

name.description: Preset name, as shown in the editor. Defaults to the matching built-in's name, numbered past any saved preset already using it.

videoId.description: Video whose current subtitle look to start from. Omit to build the preset from `captionStyle` and the style's defaults.

SaveTextPresetRequest.description: Save a personal text preset. The style starts from the given text overlay, else from the editor's default text look; every style field sent alongside overrides it.

color.description: Hex color in #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA form. Responses use uppercase #RRGGBBAA.

fontSizeScale.description: Font size relative to the editor's default (7.5% of the canvas's shorter side): 1 is the default, 0.6 a caption, 1.4 a headline. Presets are video-independent, so this is a scale rather than pixels; adding an overlay resolves it for the video it lands on.

outline.description: Outline color, or null for none.

textOverlayId.description: Text overlay to copy the style from, keeping a custom font and reading its size relative to that video's canvas. Goes together with `videoId`.

videoId.description: Video holding the text overlay to copy the style from. Goes together with `textOverlayId`.

ScreenOnlyLayout.description: Screen fills the frame or sits centered; the camera is hidden. Combi (all ratios).

screenFit.description: Only honoured when `style: "fullscreen"`. Defaults to cover.

style.description: `fullscreen` fills the frame with the screen (optional `screenFit`); `middle` centers the screen.

ScreenOnlyLayout.title: Screen Only

endSeconds.description: End of the matching transcript sentence, in seconds. Null for title matches.

startSeconds.description: Start of the matching transcript sentence, in seconds. Null for title matches.

Sentence.description: A sentence from the transcript with timestamps

text.example: Hello and welcome to this tutorial.

SetBackgroundMusicRequest.description: Set the video's background music from either your own uploaded audio (`sourceId`) or Tella's curated catalog (`presetId`), or change the current track's volume or name

name.description: Optional display name for the track. Defaults to the preset's name when `presetId` is given.

presetId.description: Preset ID of a curated Tella music track, from a `default` item of type `music` in `GET /v1/library`. Nothing to upload. Mutually exclusive with `sourceId`. Omit both to keep the current track and change only its `volume` or `name`.

sourceId.description: Audio source ID from `POST /v1/sources` (`kind: "audio"`). Mutually exclusive with `presetId`. Omit both to keep the current track and change only its `volume` or `name`.

volume.description: Track volume from 0 (silent) to 1 (full volume). Defaults to 0.2 for a new track, and to the current track's volume when neither `sourceId` nor `presetId` is given.

SetVideoThumbnailRequest.description: Request body for setting a video's thumbnail. Provide exactly one of sourceId (uploaded image) or inpointMs (frame from the video).

inpointMs.description: Pick a video frame as the thumbnail: time in ms on the video's playback timeline (cuts applied, cumulative across clips). Clears any previously uploaded thumbnail image. Mutually exclusive with sourceId.

sourceId.description: Use an uploaded image as the thumbnail. Source ID from POST /v1/sources (kind: 'image'); upload the image bytes to the source's uploadUrl first. Mutually exclusive with inpointMs.

customThumbnailURL.description: CDN URL of the uploaded thumbnail image. Only present when the thumbnail was set from a sourceId.

inpointMs.description: The thumbnail frame time in ms. Only present when the thumbnail was set from an inpointMs.

color.description: Hex color in #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA form. Responses use uppercase #RRGGBBAA.

width.description: Artboard pixels, drawn inside the outline.

color.description: Hex color in #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA form. Responses use uppercase #RRGGBBAA.

width.description: Artboard pixels, drawn inside the outline.

ShapeType.description: The outline, stretched to fill the overlay box: a non-square box makes a rectangle or an oval. `path` draws the overlay's own `path`.

SideBySideLayout.description: Camera and screen side by side. Combi (all ratios). Landscape splits horizontally (`position: left/right`, style regular/even/overlap/perspective); portrait and square split vertically 50/50 (`position: top/bottom` for the camera half, `style: even` only). Note that `even` crops the screen recording to fill its half; see `style`.

position.description: Where the camera sits. `left`/`right` on landscape clips; `top`/`bottom` on portrait and square clips.

style.description: `regular` weights camera and screen unevenly, `even` splits 50/50, `overlap` lets the camera bleed over the screen edge (and requires `size`), `perspective` angles the camera and screen toward each other (landscape only). Portrait and square clips support `even` only. `regular` and `overlap` scale the whole screen recording to fit its panel; `even` fills each half edge to edge and center-crops the screen to that half-canvas box (roughly half its width on a landscape canvas), with no `screenFit`/letterbox option. Avoid `even` for terminals, code, spreadsheets or other dense screen content unless you check the result with a clip frame. In the editor's layout picker these are 'Split Left/Right' (regular), 'Split Left/Right Overlap' (overlap, size M or L), 'Split Left/Right Small' (overlap, size S) and 'Split Left/Right 50/50' (even); users often call Overlap 'overlay'.

breakAfter.description: `true` forces a subtitle break after the word, so the next word starts a new subtitle block; `false` removes it. Leaves the word's text and visibility alone.

cameraStyle.description: The camera's frame shape, as the editor's Camera style picker sets it, overriding the named layout's own: `circle`, `square`, `portrait`, `none` (a rectangle in the camera slot's aspect, rounded by the clip's `corners`, e.g. a squircle when corners are `squircle`), `cutout` (the presenter cut out of the camera feed with no frame or room, in the layout's camera position — e.g. `camera-bubble` with `style: full` and `position: bottom-left` for a full-screen recording with a cut-out presenter in the corner; it switches pop-out off), `blob` or `blob-outline`. It shapes the camera bubble and the pop-out frame. Null clears it so the layout's own shape applies; omitted leaves it as it is. Needs a camera recording and a named layout that frames the camera (not cut-out, screen-only or custom; on a custom layout set `presentation.shape`). On the base layout it is accepted without `layout`.

crop.description: Crop the clip's screen recording for this layout only — the editor's crop modal on “This layout only”. Other layouts keep following the clip's crop; `null` makes this layout follow it again. Masks that start in the layout stay anchored to their content, and a custom layout's screen box keeps its on-canvas scale unless the same request writes `layout` geometry. Needs a screen recording or an uploaded video in the clip. To crop the recording across the whole clip use auto-crop.

popOut.description: Switch the camera pop-out on (an object merges over the current settings) or off (null). Omitted leaves it as it is, except that a cut-out layout or `cameraStyle: cutout` drops it. On the base layout this, `cameraStyle` and `crop` are accepted without `layout`.

startTimeMs.description: Start time in ms on the clip's playback timeline (cuts applied)

transitionStyle.description: Only valid on time-ranged layouts; rejected on the base (clip-spanning) layout.

intensity.description: Strength from 0 to 1. Blur: 0 is the standard blur and 1 blurs three times as heavily; the content stays fully hidden at every value (defaults to 0). Highlight: how dark the area outside the highlight goes, 0 = no dimming, 1 = black (defaults to 0.7).

startTimeMs.description: Start time in ms on the clip's playback timeline (cuts applied)

transition.description: `smooth` fades the mask in and out, `hard_cut` pops it. New masks start on `hard_cut`.

zIndex.description: Stacking position among the clip's image, video and text overlays: 0 is the backmost. `depth` applies first — a `behind_presenter` overlay stays behind the presenter whatever its zIndex — so the order only matters among overlays at the same depth. borderStyle.description: Border and shadow around the clip's frames — the editor Style panel's Border style. `solid-shadow-left` and `solid-shadow-right` are the solid shadow and its direction; `snake` and `glass` (a liquid glass rim) keep the clip's current settings for that style, else the editor's default. The layout and the camera frame's position and size don't change. Returns 400 when the clip has no camera.

corners.description: Corner rounding of the clip's frames (screen and camera) — the editor Style panel's Shape: `none` (square), `regular` (rounded) or `squircle` (very rounded). keepCameraFaceCentered.description: Pan the camera to keep the presenter's face centered as they move, the editor's Keep face centered; it takes over from `cameraFocusPoint` while on. Returns 400 when turned on for a clip with no camera or a camera without face detections (made when a recording is processed).

microphoneVolume.description: Microphone volume for this clip only, overriding the video's `microphoneVolume`. 1 is the recorded level, 0 mutes it, 2 doubles it. Pass null to clear the override so the clip follows the video again. Null and 0 are no-ops when the clip has no microphone audio. Other values return 400 when the clip has no microphone audio to control, i.e. whenever a read reports the field as absent.

Other values return 400 when the clip has no such audio to control, i.e. whenever a read reports the field as absent.

Lottie overlays share the stack but aren't listed, so listed values can skip a number. A value past the top moves the overlay to the front; the other overlays keep their relative order.

outline.description: Set an outline color, or null to remove the outline.

Lottie overlays share the stack but aren't listed, so listed values can skip a number. A value past the top moves the overlay to the front; the other overlays keep their relative order.

UpdateClipTranscriptWordsRequest.description: Correct what the transcript says. Word edits change the transcript, captions and subtitles only — they never change the audio or the clip's timing. Use cut-by-transcript to remove spoken words from the video. The whole batch is applied atomically, so a request never changes only some of its words. A `500` does not by itself mean nothing changed — the words can land and a later step of the commit still fail — so treat the outcome as either fully applied or not applied at all, and re-send the identical request to settle it; every edit assigns a word outright, so re-sending is safe.

words.description: Word edits to apply, at most one per word index and at most 100 per request. Indices are stable across cuts, but a word that is currently cut out of the clip cannot be edited.

words.description: The edited words in their new state, in the order they were sent.

emoji.description: Unicode emoji character for the group

allowedEmbedDomains.description: Restrict embedding to these domains only (Premium feature). Empty array allows all domains.

autoRatio.description: The editor's Setup → Size → Auto. true sizes the canvas from the video's recording (the first clip with a screen recording, else the first clip's video or image) with the layout's padding equal on all sides, and keeps it following the recording as layouts change; when the canvas changes ratio class, layouts are remapped like a dimensions change. false pins the current size. Pass either autoRatio or dimensions, not both.

callToAction.description: The video's own call-to-action button on its share page. Label and url are trimmed; url must start with https:// or http://. null removes the video's own button, after which the workspace's default (`settings.workspaceCallToAction`) shows if there is one. Never changes the workspace default.

captionGrouping.description: How subtitle text is grouped: sentence chunks or one word at a time.

commentEmailsEnabled.description: Send email notifications for new comments

This is the layout canvas, not the output resolution: request a 4K file with `resolution: "4k"` on `POST /v1/videos/{id}/exports`. Changing it also remaps every clip and section layout to a ratio-appropriate equivalent (clips using a custom layout fall back to a standard one), exactly like switching size in the editor's Setup → Size. No-op when the video already has the requested size. The editor's presets: 1920x1080 (16:9), 1920x1200 (16:10), 1440x1080 (4:3), 1080x1080 (1:1), 1080x1350 (4:5), 1080x1920 (9:16).

The response's `settings.eyeContact` shows the switch as asked for with `status: "processing"`; read the video until it is `ready`. Screen recordings and uploaded videos are never changed. motionBlur.description: Blur fast zoom, pan, and cursor movement. Defaults on for new videos.

motionBlurAmount.description: Motion blur strength, the editor's Motion blur slider: 0.1 (subtle) to 2 (strong), 1 is the default. Setting it turns motion blur on, so it can't be combined with `motionBlur: false`.

password.description: Password for viewing. Required when linkScope is 'password', ignored otherwise.

rawDownloadsEnabled.description: Allow viewers to download raw source files

searchEngineIndexingEnabled.description: Allow search engines to index the video page

viewCountEnabled.description: Show view count on video page

info.description:
The Tella Public API allows you to programmatically access your videos and playlists, including transcripts, chapters, and thumbnails.

## Authentication

All requests require a Bearer token in the Authorization header:
```
Authorization: Bearer tella_pk_xxxxx...
```

API keys can be generated in your Tella workspace settings.

## Rate Limiting

The API is rate-limited to 200 requests per minute per user within a workspace.
Rate limit information is returned in response headers:
- `RateLimit-Policy`: Named quota, request limit, and window in seconds
- `RateLimit`: Remaining quota and seconds until reset
- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: Maximum requests per window
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: Remaining requests in current window
- `X-RateLimit-Reset`: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the window resets

A `429 Too Many Requests` response also includes `Retry-After` in seconds.

post.description: Tell Tella that a take went wrong, so the cause gets found and fixed in Auto Capture. That covers what it filmed (the wrong page or feature, a step that was asked for missed or cut off, stopping short of the result) and how the recording came out (choppy playback, frozen or black frames, a cursor that doesn't match what happened). Reporting changes nothing on the take, starts nothing and costs nothing; to get a better take, revise it over the MCP server. A take can be reported more than once, by the person who started it or anyone in the workspace it was made in. A take that is still running can't be reported (400). Any other source, or a take you can't see, answers 404.

get.description: Returns a page of reusable media saved to the library — images, videos, screenshots, sound effects, music and LUTs — for one scope. Items added through the API include a `sourceId` you can pass anywhere a source is accepted, including images. Editor-added images, screenshots, music and LUTs expose a hosted `url` instead. URL captures from `POST /v1/library/screenshots` are placeable `image` or `video` items. Media still being generated in the editor is omitted. `scope=default` returns Tella's curated sound effect and background music catalogs instead of stored media: those items carry a `presetId` to place them with (`sound-effect` items via `POST /v1/videos/{id}/clips/{clipId}/sound-effects`, `music` items via `PUT /v1/videos/{id}/background-music`), a `category`, and a publicly fetchable `url` for previewing, and arrive as a single page; filter with `type=sound-effect` or `type=music`, or omit `type` for both. Tella's default backgrounds are not part of this catalog — they are placed as a background rather than as a source, and are listed by `GET /v1/backgrounds`. `scope=pinterest`, `scope=arena` and `scope=mymind` list the images you saved in that service once you connect it under Settings → Connections: your newest saves, or matches for `query`, as one page. Their `id` is the service's own ID; bring one into Tella with `POST /v1/library` and `from` before placing it. A service you haven't connected returns 503 `unavailable`.

Bring a `pinterest`, `arena`, `mymind` or `vintage` item in with `POST /v1/library` and `from`.

post.description: Starts generating an image, a short video clip or a sound effect from a text prompt with the same AI generators the editor's media panels use. Generation is asynchronous: the response is a `generation` whose `id` is the private library item the result is saved as. Poll `GET /v1/library/generations/{id}` every few seconds (images usually take 30-90 seconds, sound effects 10-30, video several minutes) until `status` is `completed`, then pass `item.sourceId` anywhere a source is accepted — `POST /v1/videos/{id}/clips/{clipId}/overlays` for an image or video overlay, `POST /v1/videos/{id}/clips/{clipId}/layouts` with `media` for b-roll, `POST /v1/videos/{id}/clips/{clipId}/sound-effects` for a sound effect. The finished item also appears in `GET /v1/library?scope=private`. Each generation counts against the caller's weekly AI generation allowance, which depends on the plan; exceeding it answers 403 with the reset time. A video is also charged in the workspace's AI Credits and is refused with a 403 while the balance is empty.

post.description: Brings media into Tella from a link. A public web page is captured above the fold at 1920×1080 (or, with `scroll=true`, recorded scrolling as video); a single post on X, Instagram, LinkedIn or TikTok is cropped to its embed card. These finish in this request (allow up to two minutes) and answer 201 with `status: completed`. A link to a single video is downloaded in the background and answers 202 with `status: running`: poll `GET /v1/library/imports/{id}?videoId=…` every 5-10 seconds until it is `completed` or `failed`. Video links need `videoId` and land in that video's library; everything else lands in your private library unless you pass `videoId`. Place `item.sourceId` as an overlay or layout media. Only import media you own or have the rights to use. Private pages, social profiles and feeds, and private, members-only or age-restricted videos are not supported. Use an Idempotency-Key when retrying to avoid duplicate imports.

post.description: Returns a `sourceId` and a pre-signed S3 URL. PUT the file bytes to `uploadUrl`, then reference `sourceId` from clips, layouts (b-roll media), overlays, or backgrounds. For a 3D .cube LUT use `kind: "lut"`, omit dimensions and duration, upload unchanged, then save it with `POST /v1/library` and apply the returned item id with `PATCH /v1/videos/{id}/clips/{clipId}/filters`. Use `kind: "image"` for images (no `duration`); Tella hosts the bytes for rendering, so you never deal with raw image URLs. To reuse an uploaded source in other videos, save it to the workspace library with `POST /v1/library` (`scope: "workspace"`); `GET /v1/library` then finds it from any video.

get.description: Returns the words spoken in a streaming upload source owned by the caller or their workspace, without a video or clip: for a source that isn't on any clip yet, such as an imported video. Times are in ms of source time and no cuts apply. Answers 503 while the source is still being transcribed. Takes the same `startTimeMs`/`endTimeMs` window and `view=sentences` or `view=text` as the clip transcript.

parameters.description: Only return items at or after this time, in ms on the clip's playback timeline. Defaults to the clip's start.
parameters.name: startTimeMs

schema.description: Only return items at or after this time, in ms on the clip's playback timeline. Defaults to the clip's start.

parameters.description: Only return items before this time (exclusive), in ms on the clip's playback timeline. Must be greater than `startTimeMs`. Defaults to the clip's end. Page through a long clip with windows that meet end to start.
parameters.name: endTimeMs

schema.description: Only return items before this time (exclusive), in ms on the clip's playback timeline. Must be greater than `startTimeMs`. Defaults to the clip's end. Page through a long clip with windows that meet end to start.

parameters.description: `words` (default): every word with its index, times and flags. `text`: every word with its index as plain text, one sentence per line starting with its start time, about a seventh of the size, for reading a whole long clip (finding retakes, repeats or where something is said). `sentences`: one row per sentence (first and last word index, start and end time, text), about a quarter of the size. A time window cuts sentences at its edges.
parameters.name: view

schema.description: `words` (default): every word with its index, times and flags. `text`: every word with its index as plain text, one sentence per line starting with its start time, about a seventh of the size, for reading a whole long clip (finding retakes, repeats or where something is said). `sentences`: one row per sentence (first and last word index, start and end time, text), about a quarter of the size. A time window cuts sentences at its edges.

parameters.description: `true`: also return the words that cuts removed, each marked `cut`, with every word's times in the clip's source recording (`sourceStartTimeMs`/`sourceEndTimeMs`). Use it to find footage the cuts took out, such as a retake, without undoing the cuts. Kept words still carry their playback `startTimeMs`/`endTimeMs`. `startTimeMs`/`endTimeMs` filter on the source times. Words view only.
parameters.name: includeCut

schema.description: `true`: also return the words that cuts removed, each marked `cut`, with every word's times in the clip's source recording (`sourceStartTimeMs`/`sourceEndTimeMs`). Use it to find footage the cuts took out, such as a retake, without undoing the cuts. Kept words still carry their playback `startTimeMs`/`endTimeMs`. `startTimeMs`/`endTimeMs` filter on the source times. Words view only.

Each track is analyzed once and cached; the first request for a new track can take a few seconds, and answers 503 `unavailable` if the analysis is still running, so retry.

get.description: Returns how loud a clip's voice track is over a stretch of its playback timeline (cuts applied, the same times as the transcript and silences endpoints): the peak level in dBFS for each step (0 is full scale; speech is usually above about -30, room tone well below -40; null where there is no audio). Levels come from stored waveform buckets about 5 ms long (`resolutionMs`), so a step right next to a cut can include a little of the cut audio. Use it to check what is left at a cut or to find a breath, click or filler the transcript misses.

get.description: Returns the cursor path and clicks recorded with the clip's screen recording, mapped onto the clip's playback timeline (cuts applied). Positions are percentages of the screen recording's dimensions — the same coordinate space as zoom focus points. Events during cut-out footage are dropped, and move events are sampled (default one per 100ms, `intervalMs=0` for every event). Use `types=clicks` to return only clicks. Returns an empty list when the recording has no mouse data (camera-only clips, uploads, older recorder versions). Pass `startTimeMs`/`endTimeMs` to read a long recording in windows; a window returns the same events the whole-clip response has in that range.

parameters.description: Thin move events to at most one per this many ms of playback — clicks are always kept. Defaults to 100. Pass 0 for every recorded event (can be tens of thousands on long recordings).

post.description: Split a clip in two at a time on its playback timeline, like the editor's split at the playhead. The clip keeps everything before `atMs`, and a new clip inserted right after it continues from there. Each cut, layout, zoom, blur, highlight and overlay goes to the part it sits on. One that spans `atMs` is split too: each part keeps its side, and a video, audio or sound effect overlay keeps playing in the second clip from where the first stopped. Both parts must play for at least 200 ms. Returns both clips in playback order; the first keeps the original clip's id.

get.description: Returns the words spoken in a clip with cuts applied — what viewers actually hear. Times are in ms relative to the clip's playback start. Word indices are stable identifiers for cut-by-transcript; they don't shift when cuts change. Pass `startTimeMs`/`endTimeMs` to read a long clip in windows; a word belongs to the window its start time falls in. Pass `view=text` for every word with its index as plain text, one sentence per line, about a seventh of the size: read a whole long clip that way (to find retakes, repeats or where something is said), then the words view for a stretch where you need exact times. `view=sentences` gives one row per sentence instead. Pass `includeCut=true` to also get the words cuts removed, with their times in the source recording. Answers 503 while a clip that was just recorded is still being transcribed; retry after about 30 seconds.

parameters.description: Only return items at or after this time, in ms on the clip's playback timeline. Defaults to the clip's start.
parameters.name: startTimeMs

schema.description: Only return items at or after this time, in ms on the clip's playback timeline. Defaults to the clip's start.

parameters.description: Only return items before this time (exclusive), in ms on the clip's playback timeline. Must be greater than `startTimeMs`. Defaults to the clip's end. Page through a long clip with windows that meet end to start.
parameters.name: endTimeMs

schema.description: Only return items before this time (exclusive), in ms on the clip's playback timeline. Must be greater than `startTimeMs`. Defaults to the clip's end. Page through a long clip with windows that meet end to start.

parameters.description: `words` (default): every word with its index, times and flags. `text`: every word with its index as plain text, one sentence per line starting with its start time, about a seventh of the size, for reading a whole long clip (finding retakes, repeats or where something is said). `sentences`: one row per sentence (first and last word index, start and end time, text), about a quarter of the size. A time window cuts sentences at its edges.
parameters.name: view

schema.description: `words` (default): every word with its index, times and flags. `text`: every word with its index as plain text, one sentence per line starting with its start time, about a seventh of the size, for reading a whole long clip (finding retakes, repeats or where something is said). `sentences`: one row per sentence (first and last word index, start and end time, text), about a quarter of the size. A time window cuts sentences at its edges.

parameters.description: `true`: also return the words that cuts removed, each marked `cut`, with every word's times in the clip's source recording (`sourceStartTimeMs`/`sourceEndTimeMs`). Use it to find footage the cuts took out, such as a retake, without undoing the cuts. Kept words still carry their playback `startTimeMs`/`endTimeMs`. `startTimeMs`/`endTimeMs` filter on the source times. Words view only.

patch.description: Correct what a clip's transcript says, one or more words at a time (at most 100 per request). Each edit addresses a word by its transcript `index` and sets either `text` (the corrected wording, which also unhides the word) or `hidden` (whether the word appears in captions and subtitles). Edits change the transcript, captions and subtitles only — never the audio or the clip's timing; use cut-by-transcript to remove spoken words from the video. Visibility and wording are independent: hiding a word preserves any correction made to it. The whole batch is applied atomically as a single transaction, so a request never changes only some of its words. A `500` does not by itself mean nothing changed — the words can land and a later step of the commit still fail — so treat the outcome as either fully applied or not applied at all. Every edit assigns a word outright, so re-sending the identical request is safe and settles it.

post.description: Posts the video to one of your connected social accounts: YouTube, YouTube Shorts, LinkedIn, X, Instagram (post, reel or story) or Facebook (post or story). This posts under your own account, so check the destination, text and privacy before calling it. It uploads an export with the `export` settings, reusing a finished or running one or starting one, so there is no need to export first. The account must already be connected in Tella (Settings → Connections, or Share → Publish in the editor); a 403 means it isn't, or that the plan doesn't include the export's resolution or frame rate. With several accounts connected for a destination, pass `accountId` from GET /v1/social-accounts; without it the oldest connected one posts. To post to several accounts, call once per account. TikTok can only be published from the Tella app, because TikTok requires its consent form. Returns 202 with a `queued` publication, which stays `queued` while the export renders; poll GET /v1/videos/{id}/publish for the result. To post later, pass `scheduledAt`: the publication stays `queued` with that `scheduledAt` until then, and DELETE /v1/videos/{id}/publish cancels it before it goes out. One publish per destination and account runs at a time. Requires edit access to the video.
